what: Round 5, P1 (JOC object fidelity): our E-AC-3 JOC objects against Dolby's decoder on development clips and on DEE encodes that move one variable each; the error-by-cell tool's calibration; the reset_banks A/B at a JOC sequence restart.
why: To find which of the round's suspects (core dither, SPX, AHT, the 12/18/21 kHz bands, sequence restarts, short frames, two outlier objects) explains the residual of the objects, under a criterion fixed before the data: a suspect is confirmed only when it explains at least 80 % of the residual in its own cells and a single-variable A/B moves it by at least 6 dB; above 30 % unresolved the verdict is 'the measurement could not resolve it'.
method: A read-only tap of the object path (crates/oadec-engine/src/eac3_objects/tap.rs, examples/joc_tap.rs) dumps downmix, matrix, objects and PCM slot by slot; tools/joc_qmf_reference.py --compare-tap holds every stage to an independent numpy model at 281 to 314 dB (the floor is 120).

Dolby's decoder: the Dolby Reference Player's GStreamer dlbac3dec, out-ch-config=21 for the objects (LFE then the objects in programme order) and 7 for the 5.1 core, DRC off, delay dropped; a black box.

DEE dee_ddpjoc_encoder 5.7.2.aec4fa9c-master, --input-format atmos_mezz, one master per suspect (oadec atmos-author scenes; noise written into the 24-bit samples), the data rate or the signal the only variable; every command line logged with its exit code.
SNR per object in the time domain, the reference's energy over the energy of the difference, whole clip and with the first two frames (3072 samples) left out ('steady').

tools/joc_slot_error.py --calibrate on two development dumps with matrix, timing and core faults of known size, under a rule written before the run (tools/joc_slot_error_calibration.json); frozen before any reference decode was read.

calibration.outcome: no window (24, 48) and rows_per_column (8 to 128) held: timing faults were in the right class at most 0.32 of the judged cells, and on the library clip matrix faults stayed under 0.95 in the right class or within 1 dB. The rule was not relaxed; the tool's classes are descriptions, never verdicts, and measure writes calibrated: false.

runs.clip: two copies of the spx-768 encode, byte-spliced

findings: Steady state, the objects meet Dolby's at f32 precision where the signal allows: DEE encodes of narrow-band noise at 6, 12, 18 and 21 kHz 135.6 to 137.4 dB, a steady tone at 768 kbit/s 137.0 dB, stationary tones 137.4 dB, impulses 135.4 dB; gate clips median 110.1 to 135.6 dB per clip.

The first frame: the first 512 object samples of a stream differ from Dolby's (about 40 dB in frame 0 of every DEE encode, 21 dB on the clip-gain fixture); this alone takes the fixture from 115.2 dB steady to 51.3 dB whole, and every single-object encode to 62 to 75 dB whole. The core matches there. Not explained; no candidate tried.

A JOC sequence restart: Dolby's objects go to digital zero for about 768 samples with a fade either side; its 5.1 core runs straight through and matches ours to -126 dB. Ours runs straight through: frame at the splice -5.6 dB, the 20 frames after it 14.2 dB. Clearing the QMF and quadrature banks (reset_banks) moves those 20 frames by 2.26 dB, under the 6 dB the criterion asks: not confirmed.
The restart fixture (joc-counter-restarts) restarts only in its first 375 frames, which are digital silence: the banks hold zeros there and reset_banks changes no byte. It cannot measure the suspect.

Data rate: on one wide-band noise master the steady SNR climbs with the rate, 62.8 dB at 384, 91.9 at 448, 93.1 at 576, 94.7 at 640, 96.6 at 768, 108.3 at 1024 kbit/s; tone at 384 89.3 dB against 137.0 at 768, quiet noise 86.2 against 100.7. Dolby's 5.1 core matches ours at -197 dBFS or below in every one, so the rate-dependent part is on the object path, not in the core's SPX or dither. Not resolved.
Dither: ours matches Dolby's. Turning our dither off takes quiet noise at 384 kbit/s from 86.2 to 40.2 dB and the tone from 89.3 to 84.3 dB; the 6 dB A/B moves away from Dolby, not towards it.
Two gate clips keep one object under 90 dB steady (88.0 and 89.5 dB); not explained.

suspects.core dither: eliminated: ours already matches; the A/B (dither off) costs 46.0 dB
suspects.SPX: eliminated in the core (core difference at or below -197 dBFS at every rate); a rate-dependent object residual remains: the measurement could not resolve it
suspects.AHT: not measurable: stationary and transient masters both at 135 to 137 dB steady, and whether DEE used AHT was not established (that read is P2's)
suspects.12/18/21 kHz bands: eliminated on DEE encodes (135.6 to 136.1 dB steady)
suspects.sequence restart: not confirmed for reset_banks (2.26 dB, under 6 dB); Dolby mutes its objects at a restart, which nothing in the round modelled
suspects.frames shorter than six blocks: not covered: every DEE encode is 1250 frames for 40 s, six blocks each; none was short
suspects.two outlier objects (evidence 61): not measurable: their source tracks are not on the machine

holdout: no correction candidate passed on the development clips, so the holdout was not scored; no look was taken at it. tools/joc_holdout.json is unchanged since it was frozen.
open: The first 512 object samples of a stream.
Dolby's object mute at a JOC sequence restart.
The object residual that falls with the data rate while the core matches.
A known-answer method that tells timing from core faults; without it the error-by-cell tool gives no verdicts.
